sentence_of_record: ARCH-V2 G22 / G23 READY legs, record runs at 4381e4b, independently reproduced (post-run review 2026-09-24). G23: identity HELD (tables sha256 04754dbc…, byte-identical, re-run and recomputed). Certificate B is ADMISSIBLE on both draws (utility 69.2% / 69.3%, LOAO wrong(established) 1 ≤ A's 1). P1, P2 and P3 HELD (cross-draw Jaccard 0.941 / 0.938). Holm: 809 → 736 per anchor → 671 pooled; the 19 ordered edges that lose establishment are all right-direction. MC-UNRESOLVED 22 of 920. G22 v1 validity FAILED as registered: the fresh-judge (random) mode puts f_raw_wrong at median 222.5 (central 0.99643 interval [43.9, 468.7]) against 7, and f_loao_called at median 6 [0, 384.9] against 667, with no replicate of 1,000 reaching either target (u likewise). The falsifier (a) FIRED: the registered simulator decides nothing. Design readings can re-enter only through the POST-HOC-SPECIFIED one-shot v2 (ruling 1 (ii)). P1 FAILED; P2 FAILED (merged exponent 1.88-2.02, CIs [1.78, 2.16], against 1.06 [0.80, 1.30]; the grok arm was not run); P3-P5 NOT SCORED (gated); P6 FAILED (2 of 14 anchors at D_c ≥ 0.95). P7 HELD under the post-data ruling of 97f3a1f: Meta-Llama-3_1-70B-Instruct is the unique top among merged's 4 called wrong(established) edges; the roster clause is OK on all three boards. Under the pre-data reading 'unique top on every board' it is NOT HELD (x12 and grok are one-edge ties). Merged wrong(established) overdispersion: by model χ² 53.40 on 20 models, p ≤ 0.0005 (0 of 2,000 permutations; within-anchor null p 0.0001); by anchor χ² 22.34, p 0.0465 ± 0.005 (Monte Carlo); DEFF 1.780 (ICC 0.0050, Kish m 158.3). [run 5abb79f (record runs from main at 4381e4b = ca84e44; zero judge calls), review 3ed7cbd (5 ACCEPT, 5 ACCEPT WITH; none rejected); denominators: grok 891 f / 920 u edges, 809 established, 2,811 judged questions in 14 anchors; merged 21,536 valid verdicts, 2,538 edges; R = 1,000 per validity mode; pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae, id-disjoint only; P7 scored under the POST-DATA ruling of 97f3a1f; the v2 one shot (e644a25) is NOT covered here] [v1 legs only; the v2 one shot, designs and stop are recorded separately] || v2: ARCH-V2-G22 validity v2 (fresh-judge, POST-HOC-SPECIFIED, one shot; zero calls; run e644a25 at instrument_lf16 f37145df9516b7ec) PASSES under the registered rule as coded before any real-data leg (inclusive ends of numpy's default central (1 - 0.05 / T) interval): part A 14 of 14 targets on grok_calib (891 / 920 / 809 edges; 0.99643), part B 12 of 12 on the held-out half H2 (1,409 of 2,811 judged questions, 11 of 14 anchors above the 200-row floor, fitted on H1's 10; 0.99583). The PASS is AT THE BOUNDARY: H2's u_raw_wrong target (3) equals its interval's lower end (percentile 0.004), so a fresh Monte-Carlo draw of 1,000 replicates would flip it with probability about 0.05-0.25. The simulator is not centred on the record. Its median raw wrong-direction counts are 13 and 18 against 7 and 8 on the full board, and 11 and 13 against 3 and 3 on H2; its LOAO-called counts run 7-15% low; its LOAO nominal runs 6-18% high. The targets fall inside the intervals because of the fresh judge's spread (beta-hat 5.24, sigma_eps,LOMO 0.373; fresh-draw quality share 0.921 against 0.936 in sample), and the fixed-judge mode, which decides nothing, misses 3 of 14. Design readings are admitted only as readings of a post-hoc-specified simulator whose wrong-direction counts and nominal run high. [run e644a25 (ONE SHOT, POST-HOC-SPECIFIED; main 165ffb8, instrument_lf16 f37145df9516b7ec; zero calls), review aec0a55 ACCEPT WITH W1-W6; denominators: part A 14 targets on grok_calib (891 / 920 / 809 edges), part B 12 targets on H2 (1,409 of 2,811 judged questions; 11 of 14 anchors above the 200-row floor; fit on H1's 10); R = 1,000 per mode; the inclusive type-7 rule coded at f1192e6 before any real-data leg decides; token_digest 3069666d...cdfc0 pinned at L15586-L15595] || nu grok: G22-NU-GROK-RECORD (d9f801b) independently reproduced (light post-run review 2026-09-24). A re-run from `git archive d9f801b` at master ARCHV2-G22-REC-1 is byte-identical to the committed output except the argv and started lines, and the streams file is sha256 272d1083… again. An independent log-log OLS with a within-k bootstrap of 2,000 resamples gives grok exponents +1.647 [1.477, 1.828], +1.910 [1.665, 2.178], +2.020 [1.857, 2.196] and +2.325 [2.141, 2.506] for N 2 / 3 / 5 / full. That matches the output to the digit, with 100 points per N and 0 zero-nominal draws. Reading P (1.06) lies outside every CI, and M / X (2.0) lies inside only at N 3 and N 5. G22 P2 is therefore FAILED on grok too. The frozen pair is the GROK-CALIB 920 pair of record (-3.3172 / +3.3001, grok_calib_outcome.txt L14). The 11 bound files are unchanged from 165ffb8, and instrument_lf16 was recomputed as f37145df9516b7ec. N1 of 3ed7cbd is closed. DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY: the CIs are conditional on one 12-model board, and the k 11 and k 12 subsamples overlap. || designs / stop: ARCH-V2-G22 designs and stop record runs (a5b68e6; lf16 876d01413318bd7b; master ARCHV2-G22-REC-1, R 1,000; DEV proportional supply) reproduce to the digit from their stored replicates. Under ruling 2 these are admissible only as the order D4 < D1-stage1 < D1-full and as the schedule quantities (3,990 / 14,490 / 28,980 matches). The (d) identification rates 0.182 / 0.518 / 0.654 are BELOW 0.80 but are sign-blind: the simulator does not reproduce the sign of the widener slope (validity-v2 random mode: established b1 median -0.023, 506 of 1,000 <= 0, against the record's +2.6386). plain_description.what: Builds a simulator of the arena and checks it against the board that was actually recorded. The aim was then to use it to choose a board size (number of matches and calls) likely to certify at least 9 model orderings, with a safe stopping rule that does not look at the answer key.
plain_description.why: Before paying for a large new judged board, the thesis needs evidence about how big it must be. Only a validated simulator can supply that.
plain_description.information: A valid simulator would size the next arena cheaply and justify a stopping rule. A failed one means no design can be sized this way. Result: the simulator as registered FAILED its validity check, so it decides nothing. Its error counts were far from the recorded ones, and cost grows much faster with the number of models than the planning memo assumed (exponent about 1.9 to 2.0 instead of 1.06). A separate certificate check passed. A second simulator, specified after the data were seen and run once, passed at the very edge of its rule. It is not centred on the record (it over-predicts wrong orderings), so its design readings are only an ordering of designs. No board size follows. These are planning quantities from the older question family. The item is now blocked: a re-run on real data is owed, and dropping it is proposed but waits for the author's decision.
